answer: Each identity registers one willow tier and locks 40 credits times the square of its weekly rate: tier 1 locks 40, tier 2 locks 160. A saffron panel samples work weekly and burns the bond of any identity whose output falls short of its tier. The ripple rule makes the k-th fake identity pay its tier bond plus a 25-credit filing fee that cannot be shared, so 1000 tier-2 fakes lock 160000 credits and pay 25000 in fees. A rented-output ring fails because auditors match output hashes to filing keys, and mismatched outputs burn the bond. An honest agent files one tier and keeps its bond.
